purpose: Independent loopback conformance services. These routes, vendor fields, statuses and graph nodes are fixture/example semantics, never additions to the public SDK protocol.
scenarioPolicy: Closed enum: the keys of scenarios. Unknown values fail with HTTP 400. Select with the JSON body scenario field; uploads and job/history query use the scenario query parameter. No environment variables or production credentials are consulted.

process.files: Keep all three scripts and this document together. async_api and workflow_api import only the shared startup/IO/durable-state machinery in sync_api and disable bytecode output before that import, so no __pycache__ is written beside the SDK scripts.
process.hostPolicy: Any other host is an argument error. localhost binds literal 127.0.0.1 without DNS. IPv6 binds only ::1. port 0 asks the OS for a random free loopback port.
process.workspace: An explicit workspace must be new/empty or contain a valid .bgx-sdk-conformance.json marker for this same service. OS file locking forbids concurrent processes and releases on process death. state.json and media files remain durable across restart. Callers own deletion of their test workspace after the entire restart case; no application directory or ambient configuration is discovered.
process.shutdown: SIGINT/SIGTERM stop admission, unblock active connections and close the listener; in-progress temporary uploads are removed. Final durable state/media are retained for restart. Stopping the process is not a remote job cancellation.

byteBudgets.policy: Explicit positive service test IO budgets. They do not restrict SDK operation counts, query hops or resumability.

process.media: Valid deterministic 1x1 RGBA PNG and mono 8000Hz 100ms PCM WAV are generated inside the service workspace. --video-fixture requires an explicit real .mp4/.webm; absent video fails HTTP 422 FIXTURE_NOT_CONFIGURED before job acceptance. --audio-fixture can replace the WAV using an explicit .wav/.mp3/.ogg/.flac. Supplied fixtures are copied to the service workspace; the test harness must independently ffprobe actual audio/video geometry and duration. The service never fabricates a valid-video claim or invokes ffmpeg/GPU.
process.authentication: No credentials are needed. Any Authorization or other request headers received are neither logged nor persisted. No default key, environment key or user configuration is read.

commonRoutes.response: Complete durable test state: format, identity, submitCount, jobs and media. Job inputSha256 is recorded; raw JSON input and HTTP headers are not persisted. submitCount increments for every accepted POST without deduplication, so an accidental resubmit remains observable.

commonRoutes.request: Raw bytes with exactly one Content-Length, plain Content-Type and optional X-File-Name basename. No multipart wrapper or request chunked encoding. Allowed scenarios: normal/error/rate_limit/disconnect/slow/acceptance_unknown; usage/partial-output scenarios are rejected as inapplicable. Optional delayMs controls slow upload injection.

commonRoutes.response: The exact uploaded/generated bytes with measured Content-Length and stored Content-Type. IDs must be 32 lowercase hex digits. Paths cannot address arbitrary files.

syncRoutes.request: Same body as /generate, with optional chunkDelayMs (default 20). format is closed: sse, ndjson, bytes.
syncRoutes.response: Real chunked HTTP response flushed event by event, including before EOF. Events have sequence starting at 1 and type text/usage/output/done/failure. SSE uses id/event/data lines; NDJSON uses newline-separated JSON. bytes frames contain 00 FF + JSON bytes + 80, explicitly exercising opaque non-UTF8 transport. SDK adapters parse only their selected external format; this is not the public SDK event schema.

asyncRoutes.query: Optional scenario (normal/error/rate_limit/disconnect/slow only) and delayMs inject query-only faults. Output/usage scenarios are chosen at submit. A stored disconnect scenario truncates exactly the first query response; the query count is durable before truncation.

asyncRoutes.policy: Durably cancels only queued/running jobs. A completed/failed job keeps its status and returns cancelled=false. Repeated cancellation is explicit and observable by cancelCount.

inputs.upload_id: required upload ID in this workspace

jobPolicy: pollsUntilReady is an explicit nonnegative service fault/test-injection parameter, default 1. Each real GET increments a durable query count and advances queued/running state. There is no client/SDK hop limit. Cancellation and terminal queries never resubmit. Artifacts are stored as stable media IDs; responses rebuild URLs from the current loopback port after restart. acceptance_unknown can be recovered for test inspection via GET /state jobs, then queried by its original ID without a second POST.

normal.behavior: Successful response or job completion at the explicitly selected poll count.

error.behavior: HTTP 422 FIXTURE_REJECTED before submit acceptance; submitCount is unchanged. Also available as a query-only injection.

rate_limit.behavior: HTTP 429 FIXTURE_RATE_LIMIT and Retry-After: 1 before acceptance. Does not automatically retry. Also available as a query-only injection.

disconnect.behavior: Synchronous JSON is truncated after headers. Streaming emits its first chunk then closes without a terminal chunk. Async/workflow submit returns a job ID; its first query truncates after a durable query count update. Query-only disconnect can be explicitly requested repeatedly.

slow.behavior: Wait delayMs (default 250) before replying/accepting; stop signals wake the delay. Stream chunks additionally use explicit chunkDelayMs. Neither option imposes a client timeout or poll limit.

duplicate_usage.behavior: The same final usage snapshot is delivered twice. Sync uses usageSnapshots or two usage events; async uses usageSnapshots; workflow uses metering_updates. Consumers must treat snapshots as snapshots rather than sum duplicates.

partial_output.behavior: Synchronous result has partial=true plus FIXTURE_PARTIAL and at most the first requested output; stream emits failure instead of done; async/workflow finish as failed/errored and retain at most their first artifact. A partial result must never be reported as complete success.

acceptance_unknown.behavior: For async/workflow POST and raw upload only: first fsync the accepted job+submitCount or uploaded blob+metadata, then deliberately truncate the reply. Restart preserves the original job and counters. Sync generate/stream rejects this scenario as inapplicable.

validationStatus: Implementation fixture definition only. No service execution or conformance success is asserted here. SD26 validation must wait for SD25 verification; SD27/SD28 must execute real process/socket/worker cases.
